repo.description:
### Summary

Integration creation accepted a "copy from" source integration id and decrypted that integration's stored connection configuration into the new, caller-owned record, without checking who owned the source.

### Details

The copy branch of `integrations.service.ts` resolved the source integration by the supplied id, confirmed only that it existed, and then called the connection-config getter, which decrypts the stored credentials before they are written into the new record. Neither the private flag on the source integration nor its creator was consulted. The equivalent check did exist elsewhere - the base-scoped integration service refused to hand a private integration's configuration to anyone but its creator - but the create path did not go through that service, and the Enterprise edition's integration service fully replaced the Community one, so the gap was present in both editions.

### Impact

Any authenticated user permitted to create an integration (a workspace Creator, a routine collaborator role) who could guess or enumerate an integration id obtained the decrypted connection credentials of another user's private data source, including database host, username and password, in an integration they then owned and could read at will.

### Credit

This issue was reported by [@komyunghan](https://github.com/komyunghan).
repo.summary: Private Integration Credential Exposure via Copy
